tasks.label: Triage issues and PRs
tasks.describe: Triage issues/PRs; research first; one child worktree per item
tasks.extra:
Required CI: `unit-tests` and `dashboard`. Arm `gh pr merge --auto --squash` and babysit. Do not wait on `e2e-test`, `e2e-test-tsr`, or `component-test`. Never auto-merge release-please PRs. Children must use the OpenCode v2 runtime (`opencode2`, equivalent to the local `opencode` v2 binary) with model `opencode/space-bunny-free`; confirm the model before editing. Do not run heavy local Node/build/test tasks: rely on CI for lint, typecheck, tests, and builds. Children may open PRs. Manager does not implement on `main`.

Research before you address: an issue is not ready to implement until you have read the code it names, written the expected behaviour and the verify path into the issue, and confirmed it is not a duplicate or already fixed. If the right output is a decision rather than a diff, write `research-<n>.md` in the run dir and stop. `needs-design` is a hard stop — do not implement it.

Never leave a worktree with uncommitted work: commit it on its own branch (local `wip(...)` is fine) before the run ends, and remove a worktree only after proving its branch landed (`git diff <branch> origin/main -- <touched files>` is empty).

State is local; do not commit `.herdr-desk/runs/`.

tasks.label: Babysit PRs
tasks.describe: Fix red required CI, answer review, arm auto-merge, clean worktrees

tasks.label: Self improvement
tasks.describe: One theme per night: desk health, doc/skill drift, dead code, slowdowns

tasks.label: Production watch
tasks.describe: Verify the live deploy, probe the agent, watch usage, revert on regression
tasks.extra: Read-only by default. You may verify, probe, and file issues. You may open a revert PR. You may run `wrangler rollback` only when `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CHM_ALLOW_INSTANT_ROLLBACK=1` are both in the environment, and only when service is down now — and you must still open the revert PR afterwards so `main` and production converge. Never print a secret, token, cookie, or user id. Never change a model default or a quota as a drive-by; file it.

tasks.label: Secret and workflow audit
tasks.describe: Diff every secrets.* referenced in .github/workflows against `gh secret list`; flag workflows with zero successful runs
tasks.extra: Read-only. Never create, rotate, or delete a secret — that is a human decision. Never print a secret VALUE; `gh secret list` shows names only. A workflow nothing depends on can fail forever without any required check noticing, which is exactly how `Claude Issues` failed 100 runs out of 100 unnoticed. Never disable or delete a failing workflow to make the report clean. File one issue per distinct defect with the evidence attached; do not implement workflow changes here.

tasks.label: Red CI jobs
tasks.describe: Own the CI jobs babysit must ignore; classify each as a repo defect or an external fact
tasks.extra: This job exists because `local:babysit` is forbidden to spend runs on non-required checks, which is right for throughput and wrong for ownership. Classify every red job as either a code defect (file an issue) or an external fact (record it, do NOT file a code issue). A gateway `404 model_unavailable` is external; a missing credential is a code defect. A path-filtered workflow with zero runs is NOT red — confirm the trigger first. Never touch a required check (`unit-tests`, `dashboard`); that is babysit's job. Never 'fix' an external failure by changing a model default, base URL, timeout, or retry count. Never delete or disable a workflow to make the board green. A repeated 'no change' report is the healthy outcome.

tasks.label: Stale issue triage
tasks.describe: Prune the open-issue queue: close stale-bot, fixed, superseded, and duplicate issues with a reason
tasks.extra: Close with a REASON, never bare — the reason is what makes the closure useful later. Never delete an issue. Never implement anything here; implementation is `desk:github-issues`. `needs-design` is a hard stop: a human owes that decision, so leave it open. Verify 'fixed' against the code, not from memory; an issue whose named path no longer exists is usually superseded rather than fixed, and those close with different reasons. At most 8 closures per run, oldest first. Never close a live issue just to reduce the count.

tasks.label: Docs and skill drift
tasks.describe: Prose-named dead paths, dangling knowledge-graph `related:` ids, stale or contradictory notes
tasks.extra: Do NOT duplicate the CI gate: `tests/repo/markdown-links.test.ts` already fails the required `unit-tests` job on any unresolvable relative markdown link. This job owns the three classes a deterministic check cannot reach — paths named in backticks or prose, `related:` frontmatter ids pointing at a note that does not exist, and notes that are stale or now contradict the code. Parse frontmatter and read the `related:` key specifically: `tags:` uses the same `- item` syntax, so a naive line scan reports false dangling edges. Bump the note's `updated:` date in the same change as any fix. Never edit the pinned vendored tree at `.claude/skills/pstack/upstream/`, and never regenerate `apps/dashboard/src/lib/ai/agent/skills/registry.ts` as a side effect. One theme per run; if `local:improve` would pick the same item, let improve have it.
